title: Immutable rollback artifact catalog and attestation manifest
author: Sofia Rodriguez
body:
Overview

This runbook defines the catalog format, attestation manifest, and operator procedures used to produce, verify, and preserve immutable artifacts for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended to:

- Ensure rollback operations are forensic-friendly and reproducible.
- Provide a canonical manifest schema and signing/verification recipes.
- Specify retention, evidence packaging, and roles for operator and customer-facing rollbacks.

Scope

Applies to: private-control-plane builds, runtime container images, model weight bundles, quantization artifacts, runtime configs, and migration/upgrade bundles used during stateful upgrades and rollbacks for Private Deployments. Excludes ephemeral telemetry logs (see related telemetry retention pages).

Why immutable artifacts and attestation?

1. Reproducibility: exact content/hashes allow deterministic rollbacks to prior working state.
2. Forensics: full evidence capture (hashes, signatures, provenance) supports incident investigations and customer audits.
3. Safety: signed attestation prevents accidental or malicious substitution of rollback artifacts.

Definitions

- Artifact: any binary or bundle (container image, model weights tar.gz, config archive).
- Catalog entry: a single row in the artifact catalog describing an artifact and its metadata.
- Attestation manifest: signed metadata document describing the artifact catalog for a release or checkpoint.
- Evidence bundle: packaged artifacts + manifest + verification receipts used for rollback or audit.

Catalog schema (canonical fields)

We require every private-deploy artifact to be published with a catalog entry that includes the following fields. Operators must not omit fields marked REQUIRED.

| Field | Type | REQUIRED | Description |
|-------|------|----------|------------|
| artifact_id | string | REQUIRED | Unique stable identifier: <service>-<artifact>-<YYYYMMDD>-<hash-prefix> |
| artifact_type | enum | REQUIRED | one of: container, model-weights, quant, config, migration-bundle |
| version | string | REQUIRED | semantic or internal version (e.g. 2025.11.03-rc4) |
| sha256 | hex | REQUIRED | SHA-256 of the artifact file (lowercase hex) |
| size_bytes | integer | REQUIRED | File byte size |
| storage_uri | string | REQUIRED | canonical URI where artifact is stored (s3://, gs://, file://) |
| build_id | string | OPTIONAL | CI build identifier that produced artifact |
| builder | string | OPTIONAL | team/service responsible for build |
| provenance | string | OPTIONAL | URL or identifier for provenance bundle (build logs, recipe) |
| signature_kms_key | string | OPTIONAL | KMS key id used to sign this artifact (if signed) |
| attestation_id | string | REQUIRED | reference to the attestation manifest that certified the catalog |

Sample catalog row (CSV-like):

artifact_id,artifact_type,version,sha256,size_bytes,storage_uri,build_id,builder,provenance,signature_kms_key,attestation_id
core-runtime-container,container,2026.01.14-rc1,a3f4...7c5e,124578312,s3://redwood-prod/artifacts/runtime:2026.01.14-rc1,ci-14522,serving-runtime,http://ci.company/build/14522,projects/redwood/kms/rs-1,attest-2026-01-14-rc1

Attestation manifest (schema and examples)

The attestation manifests are the authoritative signed documents that reference a set of catalog entries. Format: YAML or JSON. Required top-level fields: attestation_id, timestamp_utc, produced_by, catalog_digest, artifacts (list), signatures (list).

Example (YAML):

---
attestation_id: attest-2026-01-14-rc1
timestamp_utc: "2026-01-14T03:12:41Z"
produced_by: "/teams/serving-runtime/ci-14522"
catalog_digest: sha256:a7b...9f0
artifacts:
  - artifact_id: core-runtime-container
    artifact_type: container
    version: "2026.01.14-rc1"
    sha256: a3f4...7c5e
    storage_uri: s3://redwood-prod/artifacts/runtime:2026.01.14-rc1
  - artifact_id: transformer-weights-v2
    artifact_type: model-weights
    version: "v2-quant"
    sha256: b6d2...12ff
    storage_uri: s3://redwood-prod/models/transformer/v2-quant.tar.gz
signatures:
  - signer: "projects/redwood/kms/rs-1"
    signature: "base64:..."
    method: "kms-sign"
---

Catalog digest calculation

- Sort canonical artifact entries by artifact_id.
- Serialize minimal fields (artifact_id|artifact_type|version|sha256|storage_uri) as newline-joined rows.
- Compute SHA-256 over UTF-8 bytes and hex-encode. The attestation.manifest.catalog_digest must match this value.

Signing and verification recipes

We support two signing methods depending on deployment sensitivity: KMS/HSM signing (preferred for Private Deploys) and GPG for lower-sensitivity field operators.

KMS/HSM signing (recommended)

- Sign (example using Google Cloud KMS-style CLI):
  1) Export manifest bytes: cat attestation.yaml > attestation.raw
  2) gcloud kms keys versions sign --key=rs-1 --location=global --keyring=redwood --key-version=1 --input-file=attestation.raw --signature-file=attestation.sig
  3) Store signature (base64) in attestation.yaml.signatures[].

- Verify (example):
  1) Fetch public key from key management service.
  2) Use kms verify or a local crypto library to validate attestation.raw against attestation.sig.
  3) Recompute catalog_digest and verify artifact sha256 values by downloading artifact headers (or entire file).

GPG signing (fallback for air-gapped operator environments)

- Sign: gpg --armor --output attestation.sig --detach-sign attestation.yaml
- Verify: gpg --verify attestation.sig attestation.yaml

Operator rollback runbook (forensic-preserving path)

1) Triage and decision
   - Confirm rollback is allowed per customer SLA and change window. Check operator change log and customer notification channel.
   - Obtain attestation_id for the target checkpoint.

2) Enter evidence mode (do not modify production logs except to record actions)
   - Tag the incident in telemetry (incident-id).
   - Snapshot current running state: record node images, running artifact IDs, KV cache digests, and relevant config versions.

3) Prepare evidence bundle
   - Create a directory: /evidence/<incident-id>/pre-rollback
   - For each artifact in attestation.artifacts: fetch artifact header, compute sha256 locally, and store a verification receipt file named <artifact_id>.receipt with fields: storage_uri, expected_sha256, observed_sha256, downloaded_bytes, verification_time_utc.
   - Save attestation.yaml and attestation.sig alongside receipts.

4) Lock-change and schedule rollback maintenance window
   - Notify oncall and customer. Acquire operator approval (2-person rule: requester + approver). Record approver names in evidence bundle metadata.json.

5) Execute rollback (safe path)
   - Use orchestrator operator tool (example command):
     rwd-operator rollback --attestation attest-2026-01-14-rc1 --dry-run=false --preserve-kv=true --evict=false --evidence-dir=/evidence/<incident-id>/rollback
   - For stateful services follow stepwise model:
     a) Drain traffic from target nodes.
     b) Stop runtime.
     c) Replace runtime artifacts with ones referenced in attestation (verify SHA-256 before starting).
     d) Start and monitor health probes for 30m (SLO target: 99% success for critical API endpoints).

6) Post-rollback evidence preservation
   - Package /evidence/<incident-id> as a tar.gz and store in secure evidence bucket with immutability flags (WORM) for retention period (see policy).
   - Attach signed manifest and verification receipts to the incident ticket and customer notification.

7) Forensics and follow-up
   - If rollback was triggered by suspected tampering, escalate to Security & Compliance and preserve network captures per legal checklist.

Sample verification receipt (JSON text file saved per artifact)

{
  "artifact_id": "transformer-weights-v2",
  "storage_uri": "s3://redwood-prod/models/transformer/v2-quant.tar.gz",
  "expected_sha256": "b6d2...12ff",
  "observed_sha256": "b6d2...12ff",
  "downloaded_bytes": "412345678",
  "verification_time_utc": "2026-02-14T02:03:12Z"
}

Retention and evidence policy (summary)

- Evidence bundles for rollbacks must be retained for a minimum of 3 years for regulated customers and 180 days for standard customers.
- Evidence storage must be immutable (object lock / WORM) and encrypted at rest with customer or provider-managed keys per deployment contract.
- Access to evidence buckets requires RBAC: role=incident-evidence-reader or incident-evidence-admin and always audited.

Roles and responsibilities

- Operator (field operator / SRE): prepare evidence bundle, execute rollback, verify artifacts and record receipts.
- Release owner (team): ensure artifact catalog is accurate, produce attestation manifests during release CI.
- Security & Compliance: preserve chain-of-custody for suspected tampering and approve long-term retention exceptions.

Automated checks (CI hooks)

- CI must produce attestation manifests for any private-deploy release candidate and store them in the signed-attestations registry.
- Pre-deploy gate: catalog_digest must match CI reported digest and all artifacts must have sha256 present.
- Post-deploy monitor: continuous verifier agent should sample deployed nodes every 6 hours and verify running artifact sha256 against attestation stored in registry. Alerts if mismatches are found.

Appendix A — quick checklist for operators (one-page)

1) Verify attestation exists and signature verifies.
2) Snapshot current state and create evidence directory.
3) Compute local sha256 for each artifact referenced.
4) Acquire 2-person approval; set maintenance window.
5) Run rwd-operator rollback with evidence-dir.
6) Monitor health probes for 30m; escalate on errors.
7) Archive evidence bundle with immutable storage and link to ticket.

Appendix B — example attestation verification script (bash)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ATT=attestation.yaml
SIG=attestation.sig
# Verify signature (example using kms-verify binary)
kms-verify --key projects/redwood/kms/rs-1 --input $ATT --signature $SIG || { echo "signature invalid"; exit 2; }
# Recompute catalog digest (python snippet or tool)
# For each artifact, curl --head storage_uri and compute sha256 on the downloaded file header/body as required.

echo "attestation verified"
